fixes.explanation: Storehouses are where Joseph stored the grain (Genesis 41:48–49), so it's a fair guess. But the grain is what the people are buying. The money goes somewhere else. Genesis 47:14 says Joseph "…brought it into Pharaoh’s palace." Grain in the storehouses, money in the palace.

Right, it's false. Joseph says, "Then bring me your livestock… I will sell you food in exchange for your livestock." (Genesis 47:16) The money ran out, but the selling didn't stop. The payment just changed to horses, flocks, herds and donkeys (Genesis 47:17).
Yes. The Egyptians say, "Then we, along with our land, will be slaves to Pharaoh." (Genesis 47:19) It's their own offer, and they make it so they won't perish. I think this one is heavy, friend.

Magicians do show up in Egypt in other places (Genesis 41:8), so I see the guess. But in this passage they're not the group. Genesis 47:22 says Joseph "…did not acquire the priests’ portion of the land…" Priests are the answer.

True, and the text gives the reason right away. The priests' land "…had been given to them by Pharaoh. They ate the rations that Pharaoh supplied; so they did not sell their land." (Genesis 47:22) Pharaoh was supplying their rations, and the text ties that to why they kept their land.

That's what they say. "You have saved our lives…" they tell Joseph. "We have found favor in our lord’s eyes, and we will be Pharaoh’s servants." (Genesis 47:25) Joseph had just handed them seed and told them about the harvest, and that's their answer.

I get why you'd think that, since the famine is the whole reason for the deal. But the text doesn't say that. Joseph established the law, "…and it is in effect in the land of Egypt to this day." (Genesis 47:26) The writer gives no end date tied to the famine.

False. "So Joseph established a law that a fifth of the produce belongs to Pharaoh, and it is in effect in the land of Egypt to this day." (Genesis 47:26) The text gives no end date for it. It also says the priests' land does not belong to Pharaoh.
